A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SRA-CL research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, appendices, and checklists are available and support reliable comparison despite relocation of material.

before.justification: V2 reports original recommendation experiments on four datasets, including baseline comparisons, ablations, hyperparameter studies, sparsity analyses, and comparisons across LLMs.

after.justification: V5 retains original benchmark results, ablations, backbone comparisons, sparsity analyses, and supplementary results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Semantic user/item retrieval, attention-based sample synthesis, 20% item substitution, training losses, and backbone-only inference remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 move into the main text without procedural changes; the new caching discussion provides implementation explanation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate next-item recommendation on Yelp, Amazon Sports, Beauty, and Office, retaining the same sparse-user scenarios. Removing an alternative LLM configuration does not change dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The main and supplementary benchmark tables retain the same 13 baselines, including LRD, RLMRec, and LLM-ESR. Backbone comparisons and sparse-user comparisons also retain their comparator sets; newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V5 removes the auxiliary evaluation using Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct alongside DeepSeek-V3. The retained experiments report unchanged leave-one-out splits, full-item ranking, HR/NDCG metrics, embedding dimensions, batch size, sequence length, and training settings.

E4.justification: V2 Appendix C.2 and Table 5 test sensitivity to the choice between DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct; this analysis is removed in v5. Component ablations, intra-user synthesis comparisons, hyperparameter studies, and sparsity analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over five experiments and paired t-tests at significance level 0.01. No changes to run counts, seed disclosures, uncertainty reporting, or statistical procedures are reported.

E6.justification: V2 Table 5's Qwen results are removed, including Yelp HR@20 of 0.1275 and NDCG@20 of 0.0526. Retained benchmark scores, all 56 ablation scores, synthesis comparisons, and plotted results are unchanged. V2 Table 6's @10 results survive unchanged as v5 Table 5.

T1.justification: The task definitions and Equations (1)–(12) are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs. V5's efficiency discussion adds qualitative reasoning without a new formal complexity bound, derivation, or assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions retain the same claims about semantic retrieval, learnable sample synthesis, recommendation-backbone independence, and effectiveness on four datasets. The expanded conclusion reiterates existing component-effectiveness and inference-efficiency claims.

C2.justification: V5 adds an explanation of one-time preprocessing and lightweight training overhead in Appendix A.2. It removes the interpretation linking DeepSeek's advantage to model size and the discussion of robustness across LLMs. Appendix D.1 nevertheless retains its statement that DeepSeek and Qwen were analyzed.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.2 documents asynchronous API calls, preconstructed contrastive-sample indices, and a preprocessing-time estimate of a few hours. These are additional disclosures, not established changes to the method. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, prompts, and printed code/data access information remain.

R1.justification: Four references are added: v5 references 4, 6, 15, and 16 concern dual disentangled attention, LLM-based knowledge-graph recommendation, and embedding precision. Section 5 briefly expands its traditional-recommender framing while retaining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: V5 drops the title's SRA-CL prefix, rewrites the conclusion, removes an extraneous reviewer-style paragraph, and adds acknowledgements. It moves the algorithms into the main text and places the checklist before the appendices. Most scientific prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V5 widens the ablation table, relocates Algorithms 1–2 and several displays, and places Table 4 beside its discussion. The LLM comparison table is removed, and the @10 table is renumbered. All seven figures retain identical drawing content despite layout changes.

improvement.justification: V5 improves presentation by removing the reviewer-style conclusion paragraph and adds useful preprocessing and efficiency detail. However, it removes the cross-LLM robustness evidence while retaining a limitations statement that both LLMs were analyzed. With the primary method and results unchanged, these documentation gains and evidentiary losses do not establish a clear net quality direction.
